values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The SK Pipeline is about 40 miles of new pipe from the Kinder Morgan Tejas mainline to Freeport LNG's pipeline at Stratton Ridge, Texas. A Kinder Morgan press release from 2014 says it was built to carry 320,000 dekatherms per day for SK E&S LNG's share of Freeport LNG exports.

verifications.note: Press release describes the 40 mile lateral to Stratton Ridge supporting SK LNG Train III at Freeport LNG export facility.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet had no tag. The Kinder Morgan release names the lateral, its length, its capacity, and the export purpose.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Platts report republished by Hellenic Shipping News says the 530 million cubic feet per day Rosarito pipeline, owned by Sempra's Mexican unit, supplies feedgas for the first phase of the Costa Azul export terminal. It is fed by the North Baja system carrying gas from West Texas and the Rockies.

verifications.note: Says Costa Azul Phase 1 would source feedgas through the 530 MMcf/d Rosarito pipeline fed by North Baja from West Texas and the Rockies.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already named the terminal. The source treats the Rosarito pipeline as a whole and does not name this segment, so the tier is medium. The capacity matches the 534 million cubic feet per day on the sheet.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Costa Azul terminal is already named on the sheet. A Platts report republished by Hellenic Shipping News ties the Rosarito pipeline as a whole to Costa Azul feedgas and mentions a possible Rosarito expansion, but it does not name this segment.

verifications.note: Rosarito pipeline feeds Costa Azul Phase 1; an expansion at Rosarito is mentioned but this segment is not named.

records.researcher_notes: The existing terminal name stays. The source does not name this segment, so the export flag is left blank.

ledger.note: Searched for a link between the Zone 3 capacity enhancement and LNG. Energy Information Administration notes and trade press describe only a westbound reversal of existing pipe for Appalachian gas. No LNG tie was found.
The Seneca Lateral moves Ohio shale gas onto the Rockies Express mainline. No source ties it to LNG exports.

The East-to-West project made Zone 3 bidirectional for Appalachian gas. Trade press only mentions Gulf Coast links on other pipelines, and the proposed Illinois lateral in EIA notes has no stated LNG purpose. No LNG tie was found.
